kernel_inventory.name: order-preserving compaction
kernel_inventory.method: one block per origin row (UNA_G10_BLOCK_THREADS=256), Hillis-Steele inclusive scan over the predicate (d <= cutoff), ascending index order preserved; NaN excluded because (NaN <= cutoff) is false, matching np.where semantics
kernel_inventory.parity_argument: bit-exact by construction: output is int64 indices, no arithmetic on float payload bits

kernel_inventory.name: per-element coefficients (gravity exponential/logistic, knn exp/log/linear)
kernel_inventory.method: per-element, no cross-element arithmetic; device exp(-x) via CUDA exp() double-precision only
kernel_inventory.compile_flag_contract: -O3 -prec-sqrt=true -prec-div=true -fmad=false; --use_fast_math FORBIDDEN; double precision only (stated in the .cu header)
kernel_inventory.parity_argument: per-element so bitwise parity reduces to exp()/expm1()-class scalar bit equality, which the K1 half of the gate battery pins on boundary values; no reduction reassociation possible inside K1
kernel_inventory.note: the engine's knn branches read the GLOBAL gravity_plateau/gravity_logistic_midpoint (not the knn_-prefixed arguments); the twin mirrors this faithfully (verified by the cohort battery case)

kernel_inventory.name: ordered selection (knn sort)
kernel_inventory.method: EXACT emulation plan: verbatim transcription of numba 0.67.0's quicksort argsort (_SMALL_QUICKSORT=15, MAX_STACK=100, median-of-three, LIFO largest-half partition stack, insertion-sort finish) so the tie permutation is the numba tie law, which differs from every numpy kind on tie-dense inputs
kernel_inventory.parity_argument: the tie permutation is contractual input ORDERING, not arithmetic: an exact transcription reproduces it bit-exactly by construction
kernel_inventory.verification: matches a real locally compiled numba probe (cache=False) on 128 tie trials + n=1000 + sorted/reverse/-0.0/empty/all-equal edge cases; battery re-check on the qualification host is part of the gate
kernel_inventory.state: exact-emulation host implementation (device plan: none; sorting stays host-side in the heterogeneous composition)

kernel_inventory.name: reductions (reach, gravity sums, knn sum)
kernel_inventory.host_twin: gpu/kernels/host_twins.py :: seq_sum/pairwise_sum/vec_sum + reduce_with over REDUCTION_TREES (seq, pairwise, vec2_tree..vec16_tree, vec4_seq, vec8_seq)
kernel_inventory.method: EXACT-emulation plan: per-cell certification selects the ONE association whose bits reproduce the engine fold on the characterization battery; the certified tree then runs host-side (fastmath vector-tree emulation) or, if the certified association has no host twin, the cell stays device-bound and REFUSES until G11 provides it
kernel_inventory.parity_argument: sum association is the parity blocker class; the gate (below) certifies the association per cell against the real engine artifact
kernel_inventory.state: exact-emulation host implementation, gate-certified per cell

context_dependence_finding.finding: the sum-association class (which fastmath reduction tree the engine's compiled sums correspond to) is a property of the COMPILED ENGINE ARTIFACT, not of the Python source lines
measured: a bare @njit w.sum() probe and a verbatim local transcription of the fold body BOTH classify differently on big-magnitude cases than the engine fold does on this host (e.g. big_at_1: local bare-probe hits seq/pairwise/vec8_seq; the engine fold hits the vec4/vec8/vec16_tree family)

the engine fold run by the gate battery on this host (njit parallel fastmath numba 0.67.0 python 3.11.16) reproduces the committed n00/probe_order.txt engine-side pattern: big_at_1 reach/gravity_exponential = 9007199254740998.0 with vec4_tree/vec8_tree/vec16_tree hits and seq/pairwise/vec8_seq misses

the cohort-realistic case discriminates HARDER than the catastrophic cases: gravity_exponential = 9.628618189812515 matches ONLY vec4_seq — association differences appear in ordinary cohort data, not just cancellation edge cases
context_dependence_finding.consequence: NO local probe twin can certify a reduction tree, and a certification is valid only for the exact engine build that produced it. The gate therefore classifies per build: --emit-host-battery pins the expected bits ON the qualification host against THE engine artifact the device will be compared to, and a cell's validity is bound to that build. This strengthens the gate design; it does not weaken it.
context_dependence_finding.test_pinning: tests/tenx/gpu/test_k3_trees.py pins only context-stable facts (trees mutually distinguishable; all agree on well-conditioned inputs; big-magnitude splits the set) and refuses to pin a host-specific hit set
